findings.title: The loop of the stages is not in the plan, and the storage rules exclude what the later phases do to the state
findings.where_in_plan: PLAN.md section 2, state item 4: "This is possible because no rule of Stage 1 lets a row grow"; section 2: "Where the state lives. On the device from the build to the output"; H1: "the host does the whole call and nothing is uploaded"; REJECTED 15 (dynamic structures); OPEN_FOR_OWNER 2.
findings.evidence: Owner, D/HISTORY.md:1562: "The stages run in a loop, right? After we finish stage 1, we go to stage 2, and then after stage 2 does reductions, we can go back to stage 1." Answered yes in D/DESIGN.md A7 (lines 87-91) and section 3 (lines 516-517, "Then back to 1"). In S/final.txt the words loop, alternation, re-entry do not occur in this sense; 'Stage 2' occurs only as the go after M12 (line 485) and in line 520. Three misfits. (1) Growth. Clique extension, which the owner decided to build (decision 2, "2: build it"), grows rows: D/DESIGN.md:691-692 "sorrell3's rows go from 2 entries to a median of 37" (testbed, read). The aggregator adds fill-in (D/DESIGN.md:563-564) and is step 2 of the owner-set order (AS-012, AS-113). Indicator strengthening appends rows (D/DESIGN.md:72) and the owner names it as part of the main goal (D/HISTORY.md:2440 "additional constraints like indicator"). The plan rewrites rows in place without spare slots (S/final.txt:357, 565) and rejects any growing structure (S/final.txt:729). Its own question 2 still recommends the aggregator "written directly as steps on both executors" (S/final.txt:865). (2) Hand-over. Below device_min_nnz nothing is uploaded (S/final.txt:395), while D/DESIGN.md:264-275 puts the GPU's gain below 5e5 nonzeros in the wide phases. The plan has no host-to-device path for a state that Stage 1 has already reduced; the device build takes the input CSR. (3) Identity. 'Equal in every bit with and without a GPU' is defined for Stage 1 steps; after a return from a wide phase it holds only if that phase also has two executors with equal bits. The plan does not say.
findings.repair: Add one section on re-entry: what a later phase must leave (rows in column order without dead entries, counters, activity marks, list masks, status record), one storage step for added and grown rows (a rebuild from a state, not from the input), a host-to-device copy of a reduced state for models below the size threshold, and whether the identity rule binds later phases. Check the state changes of Stage 2 and of A8 steps 2 and 3 against state item 4 before M5 fixes the storage.

findings.title: 'Complete' can be met while parallel work stays on the host: nine ways
findings.where_in_plan: final.txt ACCEPTANCE 1 to 8 and the closing sentence on the narrow reading; HYBRID_RULE H7; PLAN.md section 1 ("a closed list").
findings.evidence: (a) Memory. H7 sends a whole call to the host when the memory plan exceeds the byte budget or an allocation fails (S/final.txt:401). H7 is not in the closed list of criterion 1 (S/final.txt:491) nor in PLAN.md:43. The byte budget has no default value anywhere. The dev nodes have an H200 with 143 GB (D/HISTORY.md:369), so no instance falls back there. Inside cuOpt the early heuristics hold about 120 bytes per nonzero (D/DESIGN.md:756) next to the plan's 40 + 32 bytes per nonzero (PLAN.md:122): 192 bytes per nonzero, 49 GB at 2.57e8 nonzeros (my arithmetic). The largest models, the owner's first target, are the ones that fall back. (b) Defaults. No criterion says it is evaluated at the shipped defaults, or that the batch order is the default. With apply_order = sequential a family "runs on the host on every machine" (S/final.txt:415); the default is decided later (S/final.txt:450). (c) Size threshold. Up to 200,000 nonzeros without consent: 50 of the 147 benchmark instances from 5e4 nonzeros (34%) never use the device; at the provisional 100,000 it is 21 (14%) (recomputed from G/testbed/benchmark240.json). (d) mirror_max_bytes, T_down and T_up have no bound of their own; only criterion 4 limits them, and criteria 4, 5 and 7 are 'proposals' to be set after M7 (S/final.txt:489, 497, 499, 503). Today 'complete' has no binding number for share or time. (e) Criterion 5 counts host seconds only "when the reduced model is delivered as device arrays" (S/final.txt:499); with host delivery the landing (2.95 s on the nine, S/final.txt:640, read) is outside. (f) Adapter. Inside cuOpt the presolve call takes 94 s against 18 s for the engine on the 240 (D/HISTORY.md:2134-2135, read; AS-282). No criterion bounds it. With the modelled 19.5 to about 4.3 s the call inside cuOpt goes from about 94 to about 79 s (my arithmetic on read figures). (g) Postsolve undo and crush are outside by scope (separate finding). (h) Narrow reading: acceptance at M10 leaves nine rules without a device form when Stage 2 starts; and criterion 8 asks for the Stage 1c gate (0.99), which the built rule set cannot meet (0.9826 on 237 of the 240, S/final.txt:518, read). (i) hash_kind = none removes 5.5% of the seconds on the 240 "without any new code" (S/final.txt:388); criterion 7 does not say which hash kind is timed, while AS-200 times the hash.
findings.repair: Add H7 to criterion 1 with a bound: zero fallbacks on the 240 and the 40 at the shipped byte budget with cuOpt's heuristic memory counted. State that all criteria are evaluated at the shipped defaults with the batch order. Bound mirror_max_bytes. Add the adapter's seconds and the host delivery to criterion 5. Fix the timed scope (hash kind, delivery) in criterion 7. Reword criterion 8 for the narrow reading.

findings.title: Criterion 7, class 2e5 to 1e6: the quoted pessimistic range is wrong and the factor 1.5 is not below the pessimistic setting
findings.where_in_plan: ACCEPTANCE 7: 'the 67 from 2e5 to 1e6 at least 1.5 times (model 2.8 to 4.0, pessimistic 1.7 to 2.3)'; 'from device_min_nnz to 2e5 not slower in the sum'; UNSURE: 'The acceptance factors I propose sit below its pessimistic setting'

The pessimistic setting of the critic is fixed costs x3, 0.5 ns per work unit, host +25%. In it the class 2e5 to 1e6 (67 instances) gives: one-algorithm as written 1.85 (host copy free) and 1.46 (copy created in the call); device-native as written 1.70 and 1.47; every step on the device 1.51 (one-algorithm costs) and 1.48 (device-native costs); the plan's own rule 1.51. The '2.3' of the plan is the 'every step on the device' variant with fixed costs doubled (2.27), which is not the pessimistic setting; the '1.7' is device-native with a free host copy. The like-for-like pessimistic values of the base figures 2.8 and 4.0 are 1.85 and 1.51. With the slope the critic used as pessimistic for the nine (1.0 ns) the class gives 1.39. Class 1e5 to 2e5 (29 instances) under the plan's rule: 1.65 base, 1.12 with fixed costs doubled, 0.85 with fixed costs x3, 0.82 pessimistic, so 'not slower in the sum' fails in the pessimistic setting. findings.repair: Correct the bracket to 'pessimistic 1.5 to 1.9'. State that 1.5 is at the pessimistic value, not below it, or propose a lower figure (for example 1.3) until M0 has measured mock steps. Mark 'not slower between device_min_nnz and 2e5' as failing in the pessimistic setting.

findings.title: Single-lock alias (R8): edges into the forest with a reservation on the binary let two lock rows alias one column; an optimum is lost
findings.where_in_plan: PER_PART 13: 'edges of origin lock go to the alias pipeline; the row stays. conflict_rule: Proposal: reservation (K3) on the binary, then the forest and the ordered fold'
findings.evidence: Model (3 binaries, exact, exact_models.py case 1): min p1 + p2; x - p1 >= 0; x + p2 <= 1; cost of x is 0. On the state of the step both rows pass R8 for x: row 1 locks x down (down_locks 1, release and force hold) and gives x = p1; row 2 locks x up (up_locks 1) and gives x = 1 - p2. The two binaries differ, so a reservation on the binary blocks nothing; the edges (x,p1) and (x,p2) form a tree, all integer with scale +-1, so both become maps. Then p1 + p2 = 1: optimum 1 instead of 0. In the design's order x is removed by the first alias and row 2 gets none (v2_design.txt line 76-77: 'Several aliases evaluated on one state hold together: each exchange moves only its own column'). A lock alias holds at an optimal point only (postsolve.hpp alias_origin_t), so two of them for one column cannot be composed. With a continuous x the forest's type rule happens to cut the second edge; with an integer x it does not.
findings.repair: Reservation on the aliased column (key = row index): one lock edge per column per step; the binary needs no reservation (two rows that alias different columns to one binary are valid together). Check in the cell table that a column whose two lock rows both qualify gets one edge. Settle with this model in the rule's review.

findings.title: Implied equation (A): a claim on the pointed row alone lets two columns turn two rows into equations; an unbounded model becomes bounded
findings.where_in_plan: PER_PART 14: 'a row takes the smallest column that points at it by an integer atomic minimum and gets its other side ... conflict_rule: Proposal: reservation (K3) on the row with the column index as the key'
findings.evidence: Model (2 continuous columns, exact, exact_models.py case 2): min -x1 - x2; r1: x1 - 2 x2 <= 0; r2: x2 - 2 x1 <= 0; x >= 0 without upper bounds. The ray (1,1) is feasible, so the model is unbounded. On the state of the step x1 has one up lock (r1) and x2 one up lock (r2), both bounds are infinite, so both units pass and claim different rows. With both rows as equations x1 = 2 x2 = 4 x1, the only point is (0,0) with objective 0. In the design's order the second column has two locks after the first application and does nothing (lowworth_v2_design.txt line 24: lock count exactly 1; line 25: 'recomputed at application'). The premise of a unit reads the sides of every row of its column (the lock count), and another unit writes one of them.
findings.repair: The unit read-claims every row that holds its column, and write-claims its lock row; then K3 drops x2 here. Put this in the cell table of the rule. Settle with this model.

Model (exact_models.py case 3): max x0 + x1 + x2, columns in [0,1], row x0 + x1 + x2 <= 3 (three parallel columns, equal costs). Exact merged column z in [0,3], optimum 3. findings.repair: Merged bounds of a class are the kept bounds plus the ordered fold (K2) of the interval ends of the removed columns; the type conditions (range of the kept column against |sigma|, the no-hole test, range_kept with its dual bound) are then conditions on the whole class or the merge is one pair per kept column per step.

findings.title: Parallel rows, subtraction step: nothing says that a target has one pivot
findings.where_in_plan: PER_PART 7: 'pairs by today's rule (of two equations the one with fewer singleton columns, then the smaller index)' and conflict_rule 'reservation (K3) on an equation that has a singleton column; a target writes only itself'
findings.evidence: design_one_algorithm.txt:156 had 'K3 on the target row and on an equation'; design_device_native.txt:175 had 'per class one pivot equation'. The plan keeps neither: it takes pairs and drops the claim on the target. With leader pairs, a class whose leader is an inequality T and whose members are two equations E1, E2 with one singleton column each gives the pairs (T,E1) and (T,E2), both with target T. Model (exact_models.py case 4): T: x + y + s1 <= 4, E1: x + y + s2 = 3, E2: x + y + s3 = 2, all columns >= 0. The feasible point x=1, y=0, s2=2, s3=1, s1=3 satisfies T - E1 (s1 - s2 <= 1) and violates the row that both subtractions leave when the core is dropped once (s1 - s2 - s3 <= -1, value 0).
findings.repair: State: one pivot per class (fewest singleton columns, then smallest index, among the rows the merge kept), or K3 with a write claim on the target row. Either closes it.

findings.title: Bound transfer to an integer root: 'integer rounding after the reduction' does not commute, because the rounding slack depends on the map
findings.where_in_plan: Section 2 K1 'Integer rounding comes after the reduction' used by PER_PART 8 'Bound transfer to the roots by the combine rule'
findings.evidence: rules_doubleton.cpp transfer_bounds rounds each transferred bound with slack feasibility / max(1, |scale|) of its own map before tighten_lower. Model (exact_models.py case 5): integer root r; child 1 with scale 1 and lower 2.0000005; child 2 with scale 1000 and lower 2000.0004. Rounded per candidate and then reduced: r >= 3 (today). Reduced first and rounded with the winner's slack or with the plain tolerance: r >= 2; at r = 2 child 2 lies 4e-4 below its bound. For row rules and propagation the rounding is one monotone function of the value, so the order does not matter there.
findings.repair: Say that a candidate is rounded by its own value function before the reduction wherever the slack depends on the source (the transfer; any rule that divides the tolerance by a coefficient); the final rounding of tighten_lower/upper is then a no-op.

findings.title: Crossing rule: 'the column takes the upper candidate' is not defined against an existing bound; read literally it moves a column out of the box that earlier deletions relied on
findings.where_in_plan: Section 2 K1: 'A lower bound above the upper by more than the tolerance is infeasible; a smaller crossing gives the column the upper candidate'; assumption 7
findings.evidence: Today tighten_upper fixes the column at its existing lower bound when a new upper bound lies below it within the tolerance (rules_bounds.cpp:38-45), and the repaired prototype applies its reduced candidates through tighten_lower/tighten_upper (fix/.../rules_rows.cpp around lines 430-455), so the column stays inside the bounds of the step's start. The plan's sentence does not say this. Model (exact_models.py case 7): x in [0,1]; an earlier step deleted the redundant row 1e4 x >= 0; a propagation candidate x <= -5e-7 arrives. Today: x = 0, the propagation row is off by 5e-7. 'The upper candidate': x = -5e-7 and the deleted row is violated by 5e-3. Singleton-row candidates are clamped in FIND (rules_rows.cpp:109-115); propagation candidates are not.
findings.repair: Add to K1: after the reduction the pair is applied against the existing bounds by the rule of tighten_lower/tighten_upper (a candidate that crosses the existing opposite bound within the tolerance fixes the column at the existing bound), and the value at a crossing of two candidates is clipped into the existing bounds.

findings.title: Singleton-column family, step A: the finite-cost guard of a substitution is a per-unit test on the cost of the step's start; the folded cost of a shared column can overflow
findings.where_in_plan: PER_PART 9: 'The cost changes of the other columns of pivot rows are folded per column in ascending pivot row'; section 2 K2 names only the cancellation test
findings.evidence: rules_singleton_cols.cpp:207-215 refuses a substitution when cost[other] - q * a is not finite, tested on the cost as it is at application; today a second pivot sees the cost the first one wrote. In a step, two pivot rows that each move 1e308 into one column pass alone and fold to infinity (exact_models.py case 6). The campaign already found a failure caused by a bound of -3e19, so extreme values are in scope. No run; derived.
findings.repair: Test finiteness on the folded sum and drop the units (in descending row) that make it infinite, or refuse every unit that feeds a column whose folded cost is not finite; add the case to the rule's unit tests.

findings.title: The reservation is not 'what a loop in ascending key gives'; it is a subset
findings.where_in_plan: Section 2 K3: 'The applied set is what a loop in ascending key gives when every premise is tested at application'; UNSURE and DEFECTS_OPEN list it as an argument
findings.evidence: Three forcing columns x1 < x2 < x3, each with lower bound -inf and cost 0; rows a: x1 + x2 <= 1 and b: x2 + x3 <= 1. Loop in ascending key with premises at application (rules_singleton_cols.cpp:461-518): x1 is applied and deletes a; x2 then has one up lock (b) and is applied; x3 has no row left. Applied {x1, x2}. Reservation in one pass: x1 holds a; x2 does not hold a and is dropped; x3 does not hold b, because the dropped x2 has the smaller key. Applied {x1}. Both results are valid; the claim of equality is false, so 'batch against sequential' comparisons (M11 gate, apply_order) cannot expect equal sets, and a loser does leave a trace (it blocks larger keys). Validity of K3 itself holds when the claims are complete (see confirmed).
findings.repair: Replace the sentence by: the applied set is a subset of that loop's set and each applied unit sees, for the cells it claims, the state of the step's start. Count the units lost per step in the gates.

findings.title: The fixed order of record kinds inside a step is not given; for the unbuilt rules the forward replay (crush) needs a particular one
findings.where_in_plan: Section 2 state item 6 and PER_PART 21: 'Records are ordered by step, then by a fixed order of record kinds, then by unit index'
findings.evidence: Primal undo of the built rules: no dependence found (see confirmed). For the designed records: parallel_fix {col, kept} adds to w[kept] in crush and merge {kept, removed} then adds scale * w[removed]; with kept of the fix equal to removed of the merge the fix must come first. A merge under range_kept is pushed together with its dual_bound, whose crush clips after the merge's sum (v2_design.txt line 83-85). Rule C pushes col_scale and then implied_integer for one column, and the crush of the conversion reads the scaled coefficient (lowworth_v2_design.txt lines 33, 38-39). An order by kind separates records that the designs push as one transaction, and K3 serialises by key across kinds. I found no cycle, but no order is stated.
findings.repair: Write the kind order into the plan with these constraints (parallel_fix < merge < dual_bound; col_scale < implied_integer), or order by unit first inside a step for the families that push transactions. Run the crush check per step in the tests, next to the stack check.

confirmed: Dual fixing by locks, all columns of a step together (PER_PART 6): the test of a column reads only its own cost, lock counts and bounds (rules_dual_fixing.cpp:38-58), and a fixing changes no lock count, no cost and no bound of another column (locks count live rows by side and sign, state.hpp:288-291). So the batch equals every sequential order; checked by reading.

Row rules as a step with the repair as built in the prototype (fix/.../rules_rows.cpp 255-490): every candidate follows from one row and the bounds of the step's start, bounds are applied through tighten_lower/upper and so stay inside those bounds, hence redundant and empty rows deleted on the old bounds stay redundant. A row whose candidate was cut stays and is tested in its own units; my runs with GPRS_BATCH=7 on the alias, merge and integer models showed no new outcome against today's order.

Bound propagation as a Jacobi round and the switch to explicit bounds as a map: each candidate is implied by one row and the box of the step's start, and the family deletes no row. Taking the best of all candidates is an intersection of valid inequalities, and a row whose bound is cut at a crossing stays in the model.

Row tightening as a map over rows: a row reads column bounds and writes only its own coefficients and sides, and the family writes no bound. Each edit keeps the row's own feasible set over the box, so edits of different rows are independent.

Singleton-column family, step A (row units): a unit removes only singleton columns of its own row, which lie in no other row, and reads costs only of those columns, so no unit reads a cell another unit writes (rules_singleton_cols.cpp:98-129, 251-300, 305-396); bounds are not written in the step, so every implied-free test stays true. The exchanges of the dual form compose because each moves one column that lies in one row. The one exception is the finite-cost guard (finding).

Step B (forcing columns after step A, reservation on rows with the column index): two applied columns share no row, so the lock counts and sides each one read are untouched by the other, and no saved row names a column removed in the step (a column in a saved row of j1 that is itself forcing shares that row and loses). Evaluating on the state after step A covers the side changes of the zero-cost rule.

Record order (step, kind, unit) and the primal undo for the built rules (postsolve.cpp:440-470): an alias names the root, which is not removed in its step once 'children of a root fixed by the transfer get no alias record' holds; col_from_rows records of one step remove disjoint columns and their saved rows name none of them; parallel_row and row_addition are ignored by the undo. I found no pair of one step whose undo depends on their order.

Simple probing with all edges sent to the forest: every probing alias holds at every feasible point (origin probing), so any subset may be substituted, and a row with an edge that did not become a map stays as a constraint. This needs the count of 'edges of the row' to include the cycle edges; today's open_edges counts only edges the forest accepted (alias_apply.hpp at edd147a7e, lines 44-49), so the counter must change with the rule.

Alias forest as the minimum spanning forest under a unique key, all trees substituted in one step by the ordered fold: doubleton equations hold at every feasible point, so the choice of tree edges cannot change validity and a cycle row stays in the model. Admissibility of an integer child reads the parent's bounds at the step's start, which only tighten (alias_forest.cpp:41-63).

Dual bound strengthening (R7) for all columns of a step together: each new bound keeps every locking row satisfied for all values of the other columns in the box of the step's start, and the clipped point stays in that box, so the exchanges compose in any order (v2_design.txt line 69). Tighter bounds of other columns only make each premise easier.

Implied integer with scaling (B, C) under the combine rule: the equation test is a fact at every feasible point, and a weak-test candidate is the only continuous column of each of its rows, so two candidates share no row and their rounding exchanges do not meet (lowworth_v2_design.txt lines 31-32, 38). A scaling writes only its own column.

Single-equation extension (E) inside one row: a column with mark +1 or -1 has the equation as its only lock in that direction, so it lies in no second equation, and the marked sets of two equations are disjoint; fixings change no lock. The reservation on fixed columns that the plan takes is never needed but is harmless.

Dominance between parallel columns (R6) under a reservation with complete claims (write the fixed column, read the absorber): applied units form a valid sequence in ascending key, and the absorber's premise (bound infinite or implied by one row over the explicit bounds of the others) only gets easier when other columns are fixed. Several fixings into one absorber are valid by repeating the exchange.

Column stuffing (S) as part of the row unit: its candidates are singleton columns of the row and its sums read only the bounds of the row's columns, which step A does not write. It is one unit per row.

Subtraction of an equation from parallel rows when a class has one pivot: an equation without a singleton column is only read and each target is replaced by itself minus a multiple of an equation that stays, an invertible row operation. Merges of the step before cannot change the core of a class that still has a member with singleton columns (a core column shared with such a member keeps two entries).

The reservation K3 as a rule: a unit is applied only if no smaller key writes a cell it reads and it holds its writes, so the applied units in ascending key each see their premise as at the step's start. That is a valid sequential application, provided the read and write claims of the rule are complete (which fails for the proposals of R8 and rule A as written).

verify:identity.summary: I read PLAN.md and final.txt in full, the validity critique, numerics.hpp, implied.hpp, integral.hpp, the fold in state_build.cpp, the device state build, hash.cpp, the budget and list code, alias_forest.cpp, the propagation and bounds rules, the batch prototype's propagation round and the CMake files of gprs, its device project and cuOpt. I wrote seven small programs in /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-acoerduek--claude-spares-spare-bsnTJo/c660eb6b-7edc-4afc-bf62-0442cb32d870/scratchpad/gpu_s1_verify/determinism_identity (fold_main.cpp with fold.hpp, fused_emul.cpp, seq_vs_lanes.cpp, k1.py, k3.py, msf.py) and ran them on the Mac (arm64, Apple clang 17); no device, no nvcc, no node, nothing changed in the project tree. findings.title: The one-pass reservation K3 is not what a loop in ascending key gives
findings.where_in_plan: Section 2, K3: 'The applied set is what a loop in ascending key gives when every premise is tested at application.' Also UNSURE and DEFECTS_OPEN ('arguments, not tests') and the validity critique, best part 12.
findings.evidence: Case: units in key order with write claims {a}, {a,b}, {b}. Integer minimum: owner(a)=1, owner(b)=2. Unit 1 holds a and is applied; unit 2 loses a; unit 3 loses b to unit 2, which was not applied. A loop in ascending key that tests premises at application applies units 1 and 3 (nothing applied touched b). In the plan's own use (forcing columns, key = column index): c0 on row r0, c1 on r0 and r1, c2 on r1; one pass applies c0 only; the loop applies c0 and then c1 if c1 is still forcing on r1 alone, else c2. Program k3.py (measured, random unit systems, not an instance set): 2 of 27 systems of 3 units on 2 cells differ; 48,341 of 200,000 random systems with read sets differ from that loop; 0 of 200,000 differ from a loop in which every earlier candidate blocks, applied or not; the one-pass set is a subset of the loop's set in all 200,000. In 28,628 of the 200,000 an applied unit reads a cell that an applied unit with a larger key writes, which the rule allows. Consequence for identity: the sentence licenses a host executor written as the ascending loop (apply_order = sequential is that loop), and then host and device apply different sets in any step with a chain of three.
findings.repair: Define K3 for both executors as two phases over all candidates of the step (claims of losers count) and delete the equivalence sentence; say that the result is a subset of the loop's. State that APPLY reads only what FIND stored, because a larger key may write what an applied unit read. Add the three-unit chain as a step-equality test and 'a loser's claim ignored' as a wrong host step.

findings.title: Row scans that are running sums today have no stated fold form, and two plan texts contradict each other
findings.where_in_plan: IDENTITY_RULE: 'one fold order for every floating-point sum (the lane fold of numerics.hpp, the ordered fold ..., a fixed tree ...)'; per_part 5: 'the drift as a lane fold'; per_part 20: 'The arithmetic of the fixed terms is today's'; section 11 switch list.
findings.evidence: Today at least 14 loops add along a row in storage order: fixed terms as a running compensated sum (rules_rows.cpp:62 and :86, rules_tightening.cpp:101, rules_singleton_cols.cpp:109, rules_parallel_rows.cpp:221, state_storage.cpp:132, :164, :288, :468, saved_row.hpp:38), plain running sums (rules_tightening.cpp:102 and :139, rules_rows.cpp:172, integral.hpp:52, state_storage.cpp:133), sums over a subset (rules_singleton_cols.cpp:330-335, rules_tightening.cpp:291-292). A device thread group can reproduce a running sum only with one thread walking the row; the per-part texts say lane fold for some and 'today's arithmetic' for the fixed terms. The switch list has no switch for it, M3 to M5 name no step that changes these sums on the host, and section 5 lists 'sums in a fixed order' as not measured. For a sum over a subset the plan does not say whether the lane is the slot position in the row or the rank in the subset. Measured (seq_vs_lanes.cpp, 11,960 random rows of 2 to 300 terms per profile, Mac): running compensated sum against lane fold differs in (hi,lo) on 11,525 rows of real-valued data, in hi+lo and in side minus sum on 0; plain running sum against plain lane fold differs on 9,330; integer data 0 in all. So stored values rarely move, but plain sums that feed threshold tests (drift, fixed size) have other bits on most real-valued rows, and 'equal in every bit' then rests on no test straddling a threshold.
findings.repair: A table of every floating-point sum over a line with its form (compensated or plain, lane by slot position, merge tree, or one owner thread with a length cap under H5), written once in the shared headers. findings.title: The work a step charges is not defined as a function of the step, and budgets decide which steps exist

findings.title: The state hash holds event counters and stale activities whose value after a step the plan does not define
findings.where_in_plan: Section 2 'The state holds no history' (items 1 to 7); section 6 'Rows: sides, alive, free size, singleton count, version, mask'; IDENTITY_RULE 'every statistic counted in work units or findings ... and the hash of the state after every step'.
findings.evidence: state_hash (hash.cpp:140-175) covers row_version, implied_lower_version and implied_upper_version, bound_changes, side_changes and the activity arrays. row_version is incremented once per event at seven places (state_ops.cpp:401, 414, 435, 466, 486, 513, 562) and is read by rules (rules_parallel_rows.cpp:452-453 tests != 0; state_ops.cpp:255 and :261 compare it with the record's version). bound_changes counts every write (state_ops.cpp:218, :317) and feeds a findings statistic (presolve.cpp:394-405). findings.title: 16-bit mask and count words cannot be combined with the atomics the plan names
findings.where_in_plan: per_part 4 conflict rule: 'marks are stores of a constant'; section 2 state item 1: 'two uint16 arrays that saturate'; per_part 1: 'one integer atomic per thread only when its count is not zero'; section 6 'mask'.
findings.evidence: Masks: list_mask_t is uint16 with one bit per list, 11 row lists in one word (state.hpp:107, 156-176), and events carry different bit sets (activity, activity_unread, side, singleton, sparse; state.hpp:193-228). Case: in one Jacobi step column j changes a bound that row i reads through an infinite side (event activity_unread, no propagation bit) and column k changes a bound that row i reads through a finite side (event activity, with the propagation bit). Two threads store different constants into the mask of row i. With plain stores the last writer wins; with a non-atomic or one update can be lost. Whether row i is on the next propagation list then depends on thread timing, and three determinism runs can miss it. Both executors are to hold 'the same arrays with the same slots', so the device has the same word. Counts: a saturating add is not an atomic add. Summing per-thread counts into a 16-bit cell wraps: a row side with exactly 65,536 infinite terms reads 0 (the activity counts as finite, rules_rows.cpp:202-203) and 65,537 reads 1 (propagation derives a bound from a rest that is not finite, rules_propagation.cpp:166-175). From memory of the CUDA programming guide, not compiled: atomicAdd and atomicOr exist for 32-bit and 64-bit integers only, atomicCAS also for unsigned short; emulating the add on the enclosing 32-bit word carries into the neighbour row's count. The plan's test list has 'more than 65,535' but not the two wrap values.
findings.repair: Masks: a 32-bit word with atomicOr on both sides, or one byte array per list (a store of 1 is order-free). Counts: the owning warp or block reduces and clamps, or a compare-and-swap loop with a saturating add (order-free), or a uint32 scratch that is clamped; where the state build counts across row boundaries, the scratch. Add step-equality cases with 65,535, 65,536 and 65,537 infinite terms and with two different events on one row in one step. Compile a two-line kernel on the node to settle which 16-bit atomics exist.

The host project exports -ffp-contract=off as a public option (gpu_presolve/CMakeLists.txt:38), but the device project imports the host library with include directories only (device/CMakeLists.txt:57-60) and repeats the flags by hand (:67, :72, :79). cuOpt globs the engine sources into its own library (cpp/src/presolve/CMakeLists.txt:7-12) and adds -ffp-contract=off as a per-source property (cpp/CMakeLists.txt:637-641) next to -march=x86-64-v3 -fno-math-errno -fno-trapping-math (:614-618); its CUDA flags (:94-219) hold no --fmad=false, and nvcc's default contracts. A device source added to that glob in M6 to M12 is compiled with contraction on unless someone adds the flag, and every standalone test still passes. Measured on the Mac (random rows and candidates, not an instance set): contraction across statements changes 167 of 2,440 candidates of implied.hpp's residual-then-divide form (fold_main.cpp); an emulation of a backend that fuses products with several uses changes 12,000 of 24,000 folded rows in (hi,lo) and 4,392 in hi+lo (fused_emul.cpp; emulated by hand, not nvcc). findings.repair: A self-test inside both libraries that fails hard: fixed inputs for dd_add_product, the candidate and the alias offset (scale * offset + offset, alias_forest.cpp:187) with stored result bits, run at the first host call and at device context creation. findings.title: The host's bits depend on the caller's floating-point environment; the device's do not
findings.where_in_plan: IDENTITY_RULE: 'For the same model and settings ... any run and any co-running load'; HYBRID_RULE: 'Nothing is read from the machine'.
findings.evidence: Measured on the Mac with the host form of the fold, contraction off (fold_main.cpp, 24,100 random rows of 0 to 200,000 terms, not an instance set): rounding mode downward, upward, toward zero against nearest changes 24,038, 12,005 and 11,962 rows; flush-to-zero changes 0 rows with ordinary values and 19,989 of 20,000 rows whose products lie near 1e-300. Kernels always round to nearest and keep subnormals. No source of gprs or of cuOpt's cpp tree sets or tests the mode (grep for fesetround, fegetround, fesetenv, flush-zero macros: no hit), so the host executor runs in whatever mode the calling thread has. A finite time_limit (presolve.hpp:149-151, tested at presolve.cpp:243) also makes the result depend on the machine and is not excluded from the claim.
findings.repair: State both as preconditions of the identity rule. The presolve entry checks round-to-nearest and that flush-to-zero is off (or saves, sets and restores them) and reports an error otherwise; the claim is stated for time_limit = infinity.

findings.title: K1 is undefined for NaN, ambiguous on where integer rounding sits, and at odds with the ordered integer image used for sorts
findings.where_in_plan: Section 2, K1: 'among values that compare equal as doubles (so +0 and -0) the smaller source index wins ... That is the result of a loop in ascending source index with a strict comparison ... Integer rounding comes after the reduction'; per_part 11 and 16: 'ordered integer image of the double, the index as the last key'.
findings.evidence: k1.py, exhaustive (measured): with NaN among the candidates 16 of 804 reductions of up to 3 candidates differ from the loop; first case (-0, NaN, 1) by source index gives (-0, source 0) on one tree and (1, source 2) in the loop. Today NaN is kept out by a return value in one place (implied.hpp:112) and by assertions that release builds drop (rules_bounds.cpp:17, :35). Rounding: integer column, row 0 gives 1/2e6 and row 1 gives 1/1e6. Rounding after the reduction stores bits 0000000000000000; today's tighten_lower rounds each candidate (rules_bounds.cpp:18) and the strict loop then keeps 8000000000000000. A host step that reuses tighten_lower in the 'loop' the plan names differs from the device in the sign of a zero bound. Sort keys: cost 0 over a negative coefficient is -0; the ordered image puts every -0 before every +0, a double comparison calls them equal and falls to the index, which is what the reviewed Stage 1c rule does (lowworth_v2_answers.txt:104-106: one quotient, then the column index).
findings.repair: K1 asserts in every build that no candidate is NaN (or drops it by a stated rule). Say that the host K1 is reduce, then round once, and that the loop wording holds for raw candidates only. Add +0.0 to a sort key before taking its integer image, on both executors.

findings.title: Assumption 25 on saturating uint16 counts is false for the old position of the activity switch
findings.where_in_plan: ASSUMPTIONS 25: 'decide exactly as today's int32 counts, because only 0, 1 and more are read and nothing is decremented'; M3 (a) with 'a switch whose other position is today's form'.
findings.evidence: In today's form the count is decremented (state_ops.cpp:28-33) and read exactly: activity_fresh tests updates + inf_count == size (rules_bounds.cpp:63) and the rebuild shifts inf_slot by inf_count * shift (state_storage.cpp:275-276). Case: 70,000 infinite terms on a side are stored as 65,535; 65,534 bounds become finite; the stored count is 1, the true count 4,466; rules_propagation.cpp:167 then takes the row as having one infinite term. So with activities = incremental the uint16 array is wrong for rows with more than 65,535 infinite terms, and the plan keeps that position selectable ('with every switch at its old position the engine is today's').
findings.repair: The count type follows the switch (int32 in the incremental position), or the incremental position is removed with the owner's word before the uint16 arrays enter (open question 8 already proposes its removal after the gate).

findings.title: The sum hash and the array comparison are undefined over leftover slots and layout
findings.where_in_plan: per_part 23: 'Per array one transform and one integer reduction: the sum modulo 2^64 of the splitmix64 finaliser of (position, word)'; M3 (e) 'step hashes over the state without layout'; section 6 'moved in without a zero fill'; section 2 'tested array by array'.
findings.evidence: Today's hash walks only the used slots of each line and skips value and twin of a dead slot ('leftovers ... are not hashed', hash.cpp:64-80). A sum over a whole array takes in dead slots and free capacity. Their content is not defined by the plan: a deleted row's entries stay in the columns 'without a write', a rewritten row leaves a tail, and device-built arrays are moved in unfilled while host vectors are zero-filled. Host-forced and device-forced runs, and two runs, can then differ in the hash and in the array comparison with equal live content. 'Without layout' also conflicts with position = slot: for columns with dead entries the rank of a live entry needs a scan.
findings.repair: Define hash and comparison over live slots only, with position = (line, rank in line); state which arrays are layout and compared only between executors that claim equal layout; or define the content of every dead and free slot.

confirmed: K1 without NaN is one result in bits on any tree and any order, and equals a loop in ascending source index with a strict comparison over raw candidates. Tested exhaustively (k1.py): values -inf, -1, -0, +0, 1, +inf, up to 4 candidates, every order and association, 158,190 reductions, 0 differ. Reason: it is the minimum under a total order on (value class, index) with unique indices.

Row-driven and column-driven candidate forms give the same pair set and source index, by derivation: a row holds a column at most once, so a (row, column, side) has one candidate and the source row is unique per column; both forms evaluate the same value function on the same bits as long as the column form filters by the row's list flag and the coefficient in the column store equals the one in the row store. The crossing rule runs per column after both reductions, so it does not depend on the form.

The lane fold has one association on both executors. fold_main.cpp: the host form (first term special, merge over active lanes only, as state_build.cpp:60-200) against a form with one thread per lane starting from (+0,+0) and the tree over all lanes: 0 of 24,100 random rows differ in hi, lo or the count, sizes 0 to 600 and 1,000, 4,096, 8,191, 8,192, 8,193, 20,000, 65,535, 65,536, 65,537, 200,000 (measured on the Mac). Rows above 8,192 entries use the same 256 lanes, so one block reproduces them; only time is open.
The six short classes are the six lane counts 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 that activity_lanes gives for up to 64 entries (numerics.hpp:153-161, read); a lane then holds at most two entries.

The lane of an entry is its slot position on both executors after rewrites, a hand-over and a rebuild, given state item 4 (no dead entry in a live row, ascending column): the fold is then a function of the row's entries and the bounds only, a hand-over is a copy, and a rebuild is decided on counters that both executors hold. That no rule lets a row grow I checked for the built rules: move_entry has two call sites, rules_doubleton.cpp:130 and rules_parallel_rows.cpp:483, and both reuse a slot of the same row.

A host without FMA hardware gives the same bits: std::fma is correctly rounded by definition whether it is an instruction or a library call, and the fold has no other fused operation with contraction off. Not run on such a host. The standalone x86-64 build passes -mfma (CMakeLists.txt:41-43) and cuOpt -march=x86-64-v3, so such a CPU stops with an illegal instruction and cannot give other bits silently.
On Apple clang arm64 the fold itself is not changed by contraction 'on' or 'fast' (0 of 24,100 rows, measured); the candidate is (167 of 2,440 with 'fast'). This says nothing about nvcc.

K3 is a function of the state: the owner of a cell is the minimum of a set of unique keys, and the applied test reads owners only. It equals a loop in ascending key in which every earlier candidate blocks (0 of 200,000 random systems differ, k3.py).

The spanning forest under a unique key is unique, and union-find in ascending key and Boruvka rounds give the same edges: 0 of 20,000 random multigraphs with parallel edges differ (msf.py); with repeated keys 9,405 of 20,000 differ, so the uniqueness of (row, substituted column) inside one family call is needed and holds for the doubleton rule (one edge per row). Levels and composition are the same: a child's map is a function of its parent's map and the edge (alias_forest.cpp:186-187), and the root key is an integer tuple that ends in the column index (:151-164).

Lazy and eager folds cannot lead to different decisions: the fold is a pure function of entries and bounds, and a reader sees a fold made after the last change if every change marks the row. In the values form the counts are never decremented and every remaining reader tests 0, 1 or more (rules_rows.cpp:202-203, rules_propagation.cpp:166-167, rules_tightening.cpp:267, implied.hpp:44-45), so saturation at 65,535 decides as the exact count.

No hybrid threshold changes which steps exist, as the plan defines steps: a family call is a loop over its list, the executor choice reads W only, the forest thresholds move where one function is evaluated, the candidate form changes the loop and not the pair set, and the rebuild rule reads counters. This holds only once the work of a step and the counters are defined as in the findings above.

Library calls of the existing device build, all on integers: cub::DeviceScan::ExclusiveScan with an int64 sum (state_build.cu:459), cub::DeviceRadixSort::SortPairs with column keys and entry positions as values (:475), cub::DeviceSegmentedSort::SortKeys on unique positions (:488), cusparseCsr2cscEx2 in a third variant (:420-447), integer atomicAdd (:250, :260, :340-354). The radix transposition sorts non-unique column keys and so rests on the library's stability, not on unique keys as the identity rule words it; ASSUMPTIONS.md:3675 already notes that. With unique keys or a stable sort and integer operators the output is fixed by the input on any GPU type.

Managed against pinned memory cannot change a value by itself. What changes on Grace Hopper is the host architecture, and there I found nothing in the engine that depends on it: the five std::sort calls have unique keys, there is no unordered container, no fmin or fmax call can see zeros of both signs (17 call sites read; arguments are absolute values or positive constants; postsolve.cpp:273-274 is outside the claim), and every double-to-integer conversion is behind a range test (rules_tightening.cpp:66-68 and :135-141, rules_parallel_rows.cpp:54-63). Stored evidence, read: hash, sizes and fixed-point flag of the node run equal the Mac run on 240 of 240 benchmark instances (commit message of 04692babd).

Recomputed from stored JSON, 240 local dumps, host runs: the crossing-rule run equals the batch run in hash and status on 240 of 240; both differ from the base run on 6 (app1-2, momentum1, neos-1122047, satellites2-40, satellites2-60-fs, supportcase12); ascending lists alone differ on 2 (neos-1122047, supportcase12). These are the plan's figures.

CCCL and CUDA documentation was not opened: the stability of cub::DeviceRadixSort, the order cub::DevicePartition gives rejected items, and the list of atomic overloads are from memory.

The prototype patch was read for propagation's batch round only; the repaired prototype of the validity critic was not built or run.

The cost and the device form of the ordered fold K2 for long runs (one thread per run or a defined tree) were not examined beyond noting that the plan gives no form for it.
Ordered dirty records for a hand-over, the memory resource and huge pages, Grace Hopper itself, a second GPU type.
Whether the stored 3,734 bit-equal device builds cover more than one GPU type or library version.

verify:performance-hybrid.summary: I checked the hybrid rule, the thresholds, the memory plan and the acceptance numbers by script and by reading, with no build, no device run and no change in the project tree. I simulated H1 to H7 with the provisional values on the recorded host steps of the 240 benchmark instances (Mac trace scaled per family to the stored EPYC node run, Stage 0 H200 costs), recomputed the HiGHS time rule from the paired runs on one machine, recomputed the critic's model of the nine, and read cuOpt's four load-balanced files line by line. Result 1: criteria 2, 4 and 6 hold together only if a real device step costs about what the performance critic assumed; criterion 6 breaks on 0 of the 240 at that cost, on 4 at 1.5 times, on 12 at 2 times and on 28 to 31 at 3 times, and at the plan's own upper figures (200 us and 3.5 ms) no threshold setting of a 750-point grid meets criteria 4, 6 and 7 together. Result 2: the reason given for H4 is measured on the 30 instances from 1e6 nonzeros, but H4 covers 84 instances; on its 53 instances between 2e5 and 1e6 nonzeros the small steps cost 7.3% of today's time on the device, not 0.3%, and six instances lose 18 to 40% of their time there. Result 3: no instance from 50,000 nonzeros is within 10% of the HiGHS time rule today (tightest: neos-1122047 at 0.75 of its allowance), but the batch prototype is 1.51 times slower on exactly that instance and above the 1.10 ceiling in four of six size classes. Result 4: H7 is not on the plan's closed list of reasons for host work, the byte formula leaves out at least 12 bytes per nonzero, and next to cuOpt's 120 bytes per nonzero the two largest instances go to the host on a 24 GB GPU. Result 5: cuOpt's load-balanced code is not built in this worktree, does a full sweep per round and conflicts with the plan's summation, candidate and ordering rules, so only its thread layout can be taken; it has no floating-point atomics. Result 6: the first device gain for a user is M2 (1.12 times on the 240 in the sum) and the next comes after four host milestones; the largest risks are the fixed cost of a real step between 1e5 and 1e6 nonzeros, the host path of the batch engine, and the device cost per work unit, which the mock steps of M0 do not measure. My scripts and outputs are in /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-acoerduek--claude-spares-spare-bsnTJo/c660eb6b-7edc-4afc-bf62-0442cb32d870/scratchpad/gpu_s1_verify/perf_hybrid.

findings.title: Steps whose device cost grows with the model, not with the step, are specified but not priced

findings.evidence: From the plan's text, priced with Stage 0 (results/stage0/fixed_costs.json) and counted on the trace of the 126 instances of the 240 from 1e5 nonzeros (5,692 steps with work). findings.title: cuOpt's load-balanced code: only the thread layout can be taken; it is not built here, sweeps the whole model per round and conflicts with the plan's arithmetic and ordering rules

findings.evidence: Read in full: cpp/src/presolve/load_balanced_bounds_presolve.cu, _kernels.cuh, _helpers.cuh, load_balanced_partition_helpers.cuh. Not built: no CMakeLists.txt under cpp names load_balanc*, the problem class or tests/mip/load_balancing_test.cu (cpp/src/presolve/CMakeLists.txt lists the built files). Per round (.cu:529-557): two graph launches, activities of all constraints and bounds of all variables, one int read back; no list, no stored activity, so a round costs a full sweep whatever changed (Stage 0: 95 to 741 us in bands A1 to B3, about 0.16 ns per nonzero, 29 ms at 1.83e8 nonzeros). The plan's 190 to 250 us plus 0.25 ns per listed unit is in line with it only for wide rounds; no list-restricted candidate kernel exists here or in the Stage 0 benchmark (microbench/README_sweeps.md, Limits). A round has 3 to 9 kernel nodes per graph, so the critic's 10 to 12 launches per step fit this structure and the designers' 100 us does not. Conflicts: sums are plain 'act.x += coeff * min_contrib' with no compensation and no count of infinite terms, reduced by cub::BlockReduce and cub::WarpReduce (kernels.cuh:47-65, 80-91, 209-222); thread counts are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 per row up to 64 entries and blocks of 128 and 1024 threads above (helpers.cuh:230-237, 343-353), against up to 32 lanes and 256 lanes in numerics.hpp:141-160; rows above 8,192 entries are summed in chunks of 16,384 and combined by a second kernel (kernels.cuh:67-142), another order than numerics.hpp. The candidate is (slack + a * own bound) / a (kernels.cuh:388-389), the form numerics.hpp:100-102 forbids, with plain max and min without a source index, a change threshold of 1e3 times the tolerance (kernels.cuh:404-422) and no case for the single infinite term. Bins are a physically reordered copy of the matrix (load_balanced_problem.cu:185-260) and the position inside a bin comes from atomicAdd, so it depends on thread timing (partition_helpers.cuh:104-141), against index-order storage with a stable partition. The graphs are built once with grid sizes from the bin offsets (helpers.cuh:379-412; .cu:346-453); a step with a list or a new partition needs new node parameters or a new graph, unmeasured. No conflict: the only atomics are six integer atomicAdd calls; the dealing 'for (i = tid + beg; i < end; i += T)' is the lane order of numerics.hpp; the fused sub-warp kernel serves five classes in one launch (kernels.cuh:17-40); the split of long columns is usable for maximum and minimum.

findings.title: Merge of parallel columns: the plan states minimum and maximum, the design has an interval sum that widens a bound

Method: reading the code and documents each finding names (rules_rows, rules_bounds, rules_tightening, rules_propagation, rules_doubleton, state.hpp, state_ops, hash.cpp, numerics.hpp, the CMake files of gprs, its device project and cuOpt, cuOpt's load-balanced kernels, the Stage 1c texts of R6 to R9 and rule A, DESIGN.md A6 to A10, the owner's messages in HISTORY.md, the register's closing rule and AS-288, AS-291, AS-307, AS-308); rerunning the verifiers' built test programs after checking by diff that their engine copy equals HEAD (crossing models, alias and merge models, integer rounding model); rerunning their python scripts over stored data (time model in three settings, the model of the plan's own rule, the nine, the H4 tail, the hybrid thresholds, K1 and K3); and three scripts of my own in /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-acoerduek--claude-spares-spare-bsnTJo/c660eb6b-7edc-4afc-bf62-0442cb32d870/scratchpad/gpu_s1_verify/amend (prototype host time per size class, memory of the nine, prototype hashes, rounds and finding counts). I built nothing, ran no device step, started nothing on a node and changed nothing in the project tree. Result: I could refute none of the serious findings; a few are narrowed (row tightening is a wording gap, the 16-bit atomics rest on memory of the CUDA documentation, the batch form of the alias transfer is a derivation because that batch is not prototyped).
